sections.h2: What is it like to sell a house in Addison, Illinois?
sections.html:
Addison is a DuPage County village where most sales involve a suburban house or condo that must clear a short list of village steps before the deed can move. The Census Bureau puts the July 1, 2025 estimate at 35,758 residents, up slightly from 35,702 in the 2020 count, so the housing stock is stable and fully built out.

The village sits on Salt Creek, a tributary of the Des Plaines River, and covers roughly ten square miles. It was first called Dunkley's Grove and was incorporated in 1884. Most of the houses date from the stretch after 1960, when developers turned farmland into subdivisions and the population jumped from 6,741 in 1960 to 24,482 in 1970. Most sellers here are marketing a house from that postwar and later building era.

The economy leans on freight and distribution. Census figures list 2022 transportation and warehousing receipts of $508,509 thousand for Addison, against $112,946 thousand in accommodation and food services sales. The village describes its economy as logistics, manufacturing and food distribution close to the interstates and O'Hare.

  • Median value of owner-occupied homes, 2020 to 2024: $341,300
  • Owner-occupied housing rate: 67.0%
  • Median gross rent: $1,245
  • Median household income: $90,431
  • Households: 12,832, with a mean commute of 25.6 minutes

sections.h2: Which village steps must be finished before an Addison sale can close?
sections.html:
Addison will not issue a real estate transfer stamp until the sewer, permit, water and paperwork items on the Community Development and Finance pages are cleared. The village page says the deed cannot be transferred before the stamp is issued, so a missed item can delay the closing date.

  • Sewer compliance: the certificate must be dated no more than six months before closing, and the inspection appointment should be set at least two weeks ahead through Community Development at (630) 693-7530.
  • Permit release: confirms no open building permits or unpaid inspection fees. A release stays valid for two months only.
  • Water: the seller books a final meter reading, done 24 hours before closing, and pays the final bill by noon the business day before closing. The buyer pre-registers for the water and sewer account.
  • Paperwork: the seller's attorney sends the village a copy of the PTAX-203 or PTAX-203A and a copy of the drafted deed.

Condominiums skip the water account and the sewer or sump inspection. The only requirement for a condo is the permit release.

sections.h2: Does a quitclaim deed or foreclosure transfer still need an Addison stamp?
sections.html:
Yes. The village issues a zero-dollar exempt stamp for quitclaim deeds, deeds into a trust, foreclosures and sheriff sales, and it still charges the $50 processing fee. A lost stamp has to be repurchased in full, so keep the original with the closing file.

The exempt stamp needs the same sewer inspection, permit release and final water bill as a sale. The village also asks for its own Certificate of Exemption form and a copy of the signed and notarized deed. When the owner name on the deed is changing, the new owner must open a water and sewer account with two forms of identification. When the name is not changing, the water balance simply has to be paid before the stamp is released.

Heirs who inherit an Addison house and want to deed it to a buyer should plan on these items even though no sale tax is due. Starting the sewer appointment early is the best way to protect the closing date.

sections.h2: What rules apply to an Addison house that is rented out?
sections.html:
Every Addison dwelling that is not owner-occupied and charges rent needs an annual Residential Rental License. The license year runs May 1 to April 30, renewal notices go out by mail in March, and renewals are due by April 30.

The village counts more than 1,000 licensed rental properties and nearly 4,000 rental units, and it grades each property after an annual inspection. For a single-family home, condo or townhouse the inspector walks the interior. In a multi-family building the village inspects 20 percent of the units plus the common areas. Owners must also attend an 8-hour Crime Free Multi-Housing class within 90 days of getting a license.

Short-term rentals are prohibited in Addison and are treated as a nuisance, which matters if a buyer plans to list the house on a booking site. A landlord selling a licensed rental can email Rentals@addison-il.org or call the Rental Housing Supervisor line at (630) 693-7544 to ask how an open license year is handled at closing.

sections.h2: How does DuPage County bill property tax on an Addison home?
sections.html:
DuPage County sends one bill with two installment coupons, and the tax covers the prior year. For 2025 taxes, the bills went out on April 29, 2026 and the installments were due June 1 and September 1, 2026. Ask the DuPage County Treasurer at 630-407-5900 for the dates that apply to the next cycle.

Addison spans Addison and Bloomingdale townships, so the township assessor named on the bill is the first contact for valuation questions. The treasurer's office says it does not set values. It also warns that a yellow box on the bill means a mortgage servicer is already paying, and a second payment would later have to be refunded.

  • The treasurer lists the general homestead exemption and the senior exemption at $8,000 each.
  • Preliminary county figures for the 2025 levy showed assessed value up 8.2%, the average tax rate down 4.37% and the overall bill up 3.83%.
  • Individual bills differ by parcel because each one falls in a different mix of school, park and fire districts.

Because the bill arrives a year behind, ask the title officer how the current year's tax and any unpaid installment will be settled between buyer and seller.

sections.h2: Can an Addison owner appeal an assessment before listing?
sections.html:
An owner can file with the DuPage County Board of Review, but only inside the 30-day window that opens when the township roll is published. Illinois law (35 ILCS 200/16-55) sets the deadline at 30 calendar days after publication, and the county says talking with the township assessor does not extend it.

The county asks for at least three comparable properties, and recent sales are the strongest evidence. Assessed values rest on the three prior years of sales, so the 2025 value drew on sales from 2022 through 2024. Written decisions usually arrive the following March. An owner who disagrees can go on to the Illinois Property Tax Appeal Board or to court. An appeal challenges the assessed value only, and the tax rate stays with the local taxing districts.

sections.h2: What state transfer tax and declaration apply to an Addison sale?
sections.html:
Illinois imposes a transfer tax of 50 cents for each $500 of value stated in the transfer declaration (35 ILCS 200/31-10). When the deed says the property passes subject to a mortgage, the outstanding mortgage balance is left out of the basis.

The declaration is filed on Form PTAX-203 or through the Department of Revenue's free MyDec system. Addison also wants its own copy of that form before it releases the village stamp, so the seller's attorney should send it to the water billing email listed on the village page.

sections.h2: What do Addison buyers look at beyond the house itself?
sections.html:
Buyers usually compare the school pattern, the commute and the age of the home. Addison Trail High School and Indian Trail Junior High anchor the public school map, and the elementary schools include Ardmore, Wesley, Lake Park, Fullerton, Army Trail, Lincoln and Stone. St. Philip the Apostle offers private Catholic schooling from pre-kindergarten through eighth grade.

Pace buses on Routes 711 and 715 connect Addison with Wheaton and other points. Census data put the average commute at 25.6 minutes, and 93.0% of residents lived in the same house a year earlier, which points to long ownership.

A seller can list with an agent, sell privately, or accept an as-is cash purchase. A cash buyer still needs the same sewer certificate, permit release and final water bill, so the village timetable applies on every route. Owners with inherited, tenant-occupied or heavily worn houses often choose the as-is route because repairs would otherwise be negotiated after the buyer's inspection.

faqs.q: How far ahead should I book the Addison sewer inspection?
faqs.a: Book it at least two weeks before closing by calling Community Development at (630) 693-7530. The resulting certificate must be dated no more than six months before the closing date.

faqs.q: Who pays the Addison real estate transfer stamp?
faqs.a: The buyer. The village page calls the purchase of the stamp the buyer's responsibility and prints the standard rate as $2.50 per $1,000 of the purchase price.

faqs.q: Do condos in Addison need a sewer inspection?
faqs.a: No. The village says condos do not schedule the water and sewer account or the sewer and sump pump inspection. A permit release is the only requirement.

faqs.q: Can a buyer run an Addison house as a short-term rental?
faqs.a: No. Addison prohibits short-term rentals and treats them as a nuisance. Long-term rentals need the annual Residential Rental License and an inspection.

faqs.q: When are DuPage County property tax installments due?
faqs.a: For 2025 taxes, the two installments were due June 1 and September 1, 2026. Ask the DuPage County Treasurer for the dates on the next bill, and check whether a mortgage servicer already pays your taxes before sending money.
